gaps: Every lesson and every question field was read; central, uncertain, product and safety claims were checked with primary manufacturer, university, research or official guidance. No one-source-per-original-assertion ledger is claimed, so all lesson records are medium rather than high.

No real acoustic measurements, amplifier bench measurements, human hearing experiments or physical speaker construction were performed. Rules of thumb and ideal models remain qualified; product specifications and local exposure rules require rechecking for actual use.
All19 Python fences executed and matched their displayed outputs;41 independent calculations passed. Other fences are equations, arithmetic illustrations and diagrams.
Inherited further-reading links were selectively fetched for evidence, not every link exhaustively rechecked; parent owns whole-project link/render/test integration.

The inherited external verification claimed several lessons high despite unsupported generalisations. This report supersedes its confidence grading; external author identity/provenance was not independently reconstructed.

diy-synth docs ask the learner to distinguish line, headphone and speaker outputs; covered in aud-amplifiers (headphone section) and module 5, but there is no worked check that a synth/Daisy/Teensy headphone output can't drive a passive speaker directly.
No coverage of 70 V/100 V distributed (constant-voltage) speaker systems.
Loudness metering (LUFS/EBU R128) for mastering and streaming isn't covered; outside the module's lesson list but relevant to monitoring.
Active-speaker/monitor calibration (setting reference SPL, e.g. 79–85 dB C-weighted for mixing) is not covered.
Ported-box design is conceptual only (no ported alignment tables or excursion modelling); the lesson defers to modelling software.
Microphone coverage omits boundary (PZM) mics and stereo mic techniques (XY, ORTF, M/S).
